question.question: What can units do in the Movment faze?
question.reference: During the Movement phase, a unit can make a Normal move, Advance, or Remain Stationary, unless that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models. If a unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can either Remain Stationary or Fall Back.

Section: 1. MOVE UNITS
Start your Movement phase by selecting one unit from your army that is on the battlefield to move:

- Unless that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can make a Normal move, or Advance, or Remain Stationary.
- If that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can either Remain Stationary or Fall Back.

After you have finished moving that unit, select another unit from your army to move, and so on, until you have done so with all of your units. Once you have moved all of your units, progress to the Reinforcements step of your Movement phase.

Each time you move a unit, you can move any of its models you choose to. The controlling player chooses the order in which to move their models. Whenever you move a model, you can pivot it and/or change its position on the battlefield along any path, but no part of its base can be moved across an enemy model or cross the edge of the battlefield. It can be moved over friendly models as if they were not there if you wish, but it cannot end its move on top of another model. The only exception to this is when moving Monster or Vehicle models; such models cannot be moved over other friendly Monster or Vehicle models and must be moved around them instead. The distance a model moves is measured using the part of its base that moves furthest along its path. If a model does not have a base, measure using whichever part of that model moves the furthest.

- When a unit moves it can make a Normal move, Advance or Remain Stationary.
- Units that are within Engagement Range of any enemy models can only Fall Back or Remain Stationary.

In Warhammer 40,000 (10th Edition), the **Movement phase** is split into two sequential steps: **1. Move Units** and **2. Reinforcements** [Core Rules p. 13].

---

### Step 1: Move Units
The controlling player selects units from their army on the battlefield one at a time to move [Core Rules p. 13]. What a unit can do depends on whether it is currently within Engagement Range of any enemy models:

#### 1. Units Not Within Engagement Range of Any Enemy Models
Such a unit can choose one of the following options [Core Rules p. 13]:
* **Normal Move:** Each model in the unit can move a distance in inches up to its Move ($M$) characteristic. No model can move within Engagement Range of any enemy models [Core Rules p. 13].
* **Advance:** Roll one D6 and add the result to the Move characteristic of each model in the unit until the end of the phase. Each model can move up to this total distance ($M + \text{D6}"$), but cannot move within Engagement Range of enemy models. The unit cannot shoot or declare a charge in the same turn [Core Rules p. 13, 14].
* **Remain Stationary:** None of the unit's models can be moved for the rest of the phase [Core Rules p. 13].

#### 2. Units Within Engagement Range of Any Enemy Models
Such a unit can only choose between two options [Core Rules p. 13]:
* **Fall Back:** Each model in the unit can move up to its Move ($M$) characteristic. Models can move within Engagement Range of enemy models during this move, but cannot end the move within Engagement Range of any enemy models (if this is not possible, the unit cannot Fall Back). The unit cannot shoot or declare a charge in the same turn [Core Rules p. 13, 14].
* **Remain Stationary:** None of the unit's models are moved [Core Rules p. 13].

---

### Transport Interactions (Embarking & Disembarking)
During the Move Units step, units can also interact with friendly Transports:

* **Disembark:** A unit that starts the Movement phase embarked in a Transport can disembark before or after the Transport moves (unless the Transport has Advanced or Fallen Back) [Core Rules p. 17]:
  * Disembarking models must be placed wholly within 3" of the Transport and not within Engagement Range of enemy models [Core Rules p. 17].
  * If the unit disembarks before the Transport moves (or if the Transport Remained Stationary), it can act normally (make a Normal move, Advance, shoot, charge, fight), but cannot choose to Remain Stationary [Core Rules p. 17].
  * If it disembarks after the Transport makes a Normal move, the unit counts as having made a Normal move; it cannot move further in this phase or declare a charge this turn, but can otherwise act normally [Core Rules p. 17].
* **Embark:** If a unit makes a Normal, Advance, or Fall Back move and every model in the unit ends that move within 3" of a friendly Transport, it can embark into that Transport (provided it did not disembark in the same phase) [Core Rules p. 17].

---

### Step 2: Reinforcements
Once all units on the battlefield that the player wishes to move have finished moving, the phase moves to the Reinforcements step [Core Rules p. 13, 16]:

* **Arrive from Reserves:** The player can select one or more Reserves units from their army and set them up on the battlefield, one at a time, according to the rules that placed them in Reserves (such as *Deep Strike*) [Core Rules p. 16].
* **Restrictions & Effects:** Units arriving from Reserves count as having made a Normal move in the turn they are set up; they cannot move further during this phase, but can otherwise act normally later in the turn (shoot, declare a charge, fight) [Core Rules p. 16].

Once all desired Reserves units have been set up, the Movement phase ends [Core Rules p. 16].

Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force.

- **Unit names are not unique** (1 680 datasheets, 1 291 names): the same name can exist in several factions or
  sources. Filter by `factionId` when it matters, and say which one you used.
- **A broad name is a category, not a unit.** "A Space Marine" is not a datasheet name: `name LIKE '%Space Marine%'`

- **A characteristic belongs to a model profile, not to a unit.** A datasheet can have profiles of different values
  (a sergeant and a heavier veteran, for example): keep each profile's name in a category result, so that a unit
  that is an exception for one profile is not given that value as a whole (example 2).
- **Warhammer Legends and Forge World.** A datasheet's source tells where it comes from: `source.name` ends with

- **Editions are per record.** `source.edition` is `'11'`, `'10'`, or `'0'` (no edition recorded: Legends and Forge
  World packs). Two datasheets have no source (`sourceId` empty). `stratagems`, `detachments`, `enhancements` and
  `abilities` have no source column: their edition is not recorded. The Core Rules rulebook is 10th edition.
- **Abilities are in two places.** Core and Faction abilities have an `abilityId` and their text in `abilities`; the
  others (`Datasheet`, `Wargear`, …) have an empty `abilityId` and their text in `datasheets_abilities.description`.

  `(SELECT DISTINCT Id, name, description FROM abilities)`, never on `Id` alone (example 4).

  datasheets in `datasheets_stratagems`; rows whose `type` reads like the rulebook's labels (`Core – Wargear

1. A unit's model profiles, with its faction and source:

```sql
       s.name AS source, s.edition
FROM datasheets d
JOIN factions f ON f.Id = d.factionId
JOIN datasheets_models m ON m.DatasheetId = d.Id
LEFT JOIN source s ON s.Id = d.sourceId
WHERE d.name = 'Intercessor Squad' AND d.factionId = 'SM'
ORDER BY CAST(m.line AS INTEGER);
```

2. A category: Space Marine Battleline units, Legends excluded. Use one query for representative units across

```sql
WITH category_profiles AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT d.Id, d.name, s.name AS source, s.edition,
                  m.line, m.name AS model, m.t
  FROM datasheets d
  JOIN datasheets_models m ON m.DatasheetId = d.Id
  LEFT JOIN source s ON s.Id = d.sourceId
  WHERE d.factionId = 'SM'
    AND d.Id IN (SELECT DatasheetId FROM datasheets_keywords WHERE keyword = 'Battleline')
    AND (s.name IS NULL OR s.name NOT LIKE '%(Warhammer Legends)%')
),
unit_variants AS (
  SELECT Id, COUNT(DISTINCT t) AS toughness_values
  FROM category_profiles
  GROUP BY Id
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT p.Id, p.name, p.source, p.edition, p.t,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
           PARTITION BY p.t
           ORDER BY v.toughness_values DESC, p.name, p.Id
         ) AS representative
  FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT Id, name, source, edition, t FROM category_profiles
  ) p
  JOIN unit_variants v ON v.Id = p.Id
),
selected AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT Id, name, source, edition
  FROM ranked
  WHERE representative <= 2
)
SELECT s.Id, s.name, s.source, s.edition,
       GROUP_CONCAT(p.model || ': T' || p.t, '; ') AS profiles
FROM selected s
JOIN category_profiles p ON p.Id = s.Id
GROUP BY s.Id, s.name, s.source, s.edition
ORDER BY s.name, s.Id;
```

```sql
WITH profiles AS (

  FROM datasheets d
  JOIN datasheets_models m ON m.DatasheetId = d.Id
  LEFT JOIN source s ON s.Id = d.sourceId

    AND (s.name IS NULL OR s.name NOT LIKE '%(Warhammer Legends)%')
)
SELECT source_id, source, edition, t, COUNT(*) AS model_profiles, COUNT(DISTINCT Id) AS datasheets
FROM profiles
GROUP BY source_id, source, edition, t
ORDER BY source, edition, CAST(t AS INTEGER), t;
```

```sql

FROM datasheets_abilities da

WHERE da.DatasheetId = '000000070'  -- Tactical Squad (SM)
ORDER BY CAST(da.line AS INTEGER);
```

```sql
FROM stratagems
WHERE name = 'GRENADE' AND FactionId = '';
```

```sql
FROM datasheets d
```

```sql

FROM datasheets d

LEFT JOIN detachments dt ON dt.Id = s.detachmentId
WHERE d.Id = '000001157'  -- Intercessor Squad (SM)
ORDER BY dt.type, s.detachment, s.name;
```

7. A unit's keywords:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT keyword, model, isFactionKeyword
FROM datasheets_keywords
WHERE DatasheetId = '000000070'  -- Tactical Squad (SM)
ORDER BY isFactionKeyword DESC, keyword;
```

```sql

FROM detachments dt
LEFT JOIN detachment_abilities da ON da.detachmentId = dt.Id
WHERE dt.factionId = 'SM'
ORDER BY dt.name;
```

9. The units a leader can lead:

```sql

FROM datasheets leader
JOIN datasheets_leader l ON l.LeaderId = leader.Id
JOIN datasheets attached ON attached.Id = l.attachedId
WHERE leader.Id = '000000073'  -- Captain (SM)
ORDER BY attached.name;
```

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT description AS unit_size, cost
FROM datasheets_models_cost
WHERE DatasheetId = '000001157' AND cost != ''  -- Intercessor Squad (SM)
ORDER BY CAST(cost AS INTEGER);
```

[Core Rules p. 13] (page footer p. 13: CORE RULES | MOVEMENT PHASE)
Section: MOVEMENT PHASE
The ground shakes to the tread of marching feet and the growl of engines as armies advance across the battlefield and vie for advantageous positions.

[Core Rules p. 10] (page footer p. 10: CORE RULES | THE BATTLE ROUND)
Figure label: COMMAND PHASE
Section: THE BATTLE ROUND > MOVEMENT PHASE
Your units manoeuvre across the battlefield and reinforcements enter the fray.

[Core Rules p. 13] (page footer p. 13: CORE RULES | MOVEMENT PHASE)
Section: NORMAL MOVES
When a unit makes a Normal move, each model in that unit can move a distance in inches less than or equal to its Move (M) characteristic, but no model can be moved within Engagement Range of any enemy models (pg 7).

- Normal Move: Models move up to M".
- Cannot move within Engagement Range of any enemy models.

Your Movement phase is split into two steps. First you can move your units, then you can set up reinforcements.

[Core Rules p. 16] (page footer p. 16: CORE RULES | MOVEMENT PHASE)
Section: 2. REINFORCEMENTS
Some units have a rule that allows them to start the battle in Reserves, such as Deep Strike (pg 39). Such units will arrive later in the battle and are known as Reserves units. Any Reserves units that have not been set up on the battlefield when the battle ends count as having been destroyed.

In the Reinforcements step of your Movement phase, if you have any Reserves units in your army, you can select one or more of them and set them up on the battlefield, one at a time. Once all your Reserves units that you wish to set up this turn have been set up, your Movement phase ends and you progress to your Shooting phase.

Details of how to set up Reserves units are described in the same rules that enabled the unit to be set up in Reserves. These rules will typically specify a distance away from all enemy models; whenever such a distance is specified, it always applies to the horizontal distance, even though normally you measure to and from the closest part of a model's base.

Reserves units always count as having made a Normal move in the turn they are set up on the battlefield, and so cannot move further during this phase. Otherwise, units set up in this way can act normally this turn (shoot, declare a charge, fight, etc.).

[Core Rules p. 13] (page footer p. 13: CORE RULES | MOVEMENT PHASE)
Section: 1. MOVE UNITS
Start your Movement phase by selecting one unit from your army that is on the battlefield to move:

- Unless that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can make a Normal move, or Advance, or Remain Stationary.
- If that unit is within Engagement Range of any enemy models, it can either Remain Stationary or Fall Back.

After you have finished moving that unit, select another unit from your army to move, and so on, until you have done so with all of your units. Once you have moved all of your units, progress to the Reinforcements step of your Movement phase.

Each time you move a unit, you can move any of its models you choose to. The controlling player chooses the order in which to move their models. Whenever you move a model, you can pivot it and/or change its position on the battlefield along any path, but no part of its base can be moved across an enemy model or cross the edge of the battlefield. It can be moved over friendly models as if they were not there if you wish, but it cannot end its move on top of another model. The only exception to this is when moving Monster or Vehicle models; such models cannot be moved over other friendly Monster or Vehicle models and must be moved around them instead. The distance a model moves is measured using the part of its base that moves furthest along its path. If a model does not have a base, measure using whichever part of that model moves the furthest.

[Core Rules p. 17] (page footer p. 17: CORE RULES | TRANSPORTS)
Section: DISEMBARK
If a unit from your army starts your Movement phase embarked within a Transport model, that unit can disembark in that phase.

When a unit disembarks from a Transport model, set it up on the battlefield so that it is wholly within 3" of that Transport model and not within Engagement Range of any enemy models. If, for any reason, a disembarking model cannot be set up, that model's unit cannot disembark.

Units that disembark from a Transport model that either Remained Stationary this phase or has not yet made a Normal, Advance or Fall Back move this phase can then act normally (make a Normal move, Advance, shoot, declare a charge, fight, etc.) in the remainder of the turn. Such a disembarking unit cannot choose to Remain Stationary.

Units that disembark from a Transport model that made a Normal move this phase count as having made a Normal move themselves; they cannot move further during this phase. Such a unit also cannot declare a charge in the same turn, but can otherwise act normally in the remainder of the turn.

Units cannot disembark from a Transport model that either Advanced or Fell Back this turn.

Section: Introduction

2 MOVEMENT PHASE

5 FIGHT PHASE

In a game as wide-ranging as Warhammer 40,000, there may be times when you are not sure exactly how to resolve a situation that has come up during play. When this happens, have a quick chat with your opponent and apply the solution that makes the most sense to both of you (or seems the most fun!). If no single solution presents itself, you and your opponent should roll off, and whoever rolls highest gets to choose what happens. Then you can get on with the fighting!

In Warhammer 40,000 (10th Edition), the **Movement phase** is split into two sequential steps: **1. Move Units** and **2. Reinforcements** [Core Rules p. 13].

---

### Step 1: Move Units
The controlling player selects units from their army on the battlefield one at a time to move [Core Rules p. 13]. What a unit can do depends on whether it is currently within Engagement Range of any enemy models:

#### 1. Units Not Within Engagement Range of Any Enemy Models
Such a unit can choose one of the following options [Core Rules p. 13]:
* **Normal Move:** Each model in the unit can move a distance in inches up to its Move ($M$) characteristic. No model can move within Engagement Range of any enemy models [Core Rules p. 13].
* **Advance:** Roll one D6 and add the result to the Move characteristic of each model in the unit until the end of the phase. Each model can move up to this total distance ($M + \text{D6}"$), but cannot move within Engagement Range of enemy models. The unit cannot shoot or declare a charge in the same turn [Core Rules p. 13, 14].
* **Remain Stationary:** None of the unit's models can be moved for the rest of the phase [Core Rules p. 13].

#### 2. Units Within Engagement Range of Any Enemy Models
Such a unit can only choose between two options [Core Rules p. 13]:
* **Fall Back:** Each model in the unit can move up to its Move ($M$) characteristic. Models can move within Engagement Range of enemy models during this move, but cannot end the move within Engagement Range of any enemy models (if this is not possible, the unit cannot Fall Back). The unit cannot shoot or declare a charge in the same turn [Core Rules p. 13, 14].
* **Remain Stationary:** None of the unit's models are moved [Core Rules p. 13].

---

### Transport Interactions (Embarking & Disembarking)
During the Move Units step, units can also interact with friendly Transports:

* **Disembark:** A unit that starts the Movement phase embarked in a Transport can disembark before or after the Transport moves (unless the Transport has Advanced or Fallen Back) [Core Rules p. 17]:
  * Disembarking models must be placed wholly within 3" of the Transport and not within Engagement Range of enemy models [Core Rules p. 17].
  * If the unit disembarks before the Transport moves (or if the Transport Remained Stationary), it can act normally (make a Normal move, Advance, shoot, charge, fight), but cannot choose to Remain Stationary [Core Rules p. 17].
  * If it disembarks after the Transport makes a Normal move, the unit counts as having made a Normal move; it cannot move further in this phase or declare a charge this turn, but can otherwise act normally [Core Rules p. 17].
* **Embark:** If a unit makes a Normal, Advance, or Fall Back move and every model in the unit ends that move within 3" of a friendly Transport, it can embark into that Transport (provided it did not disembark in the same phase) [Core Rules p. 17].

---

### Step 2: Reinforcements
Once all units on the battlefield that the player wishes to move have finished moving, the phase moves to the Reinforcements step [Core Rules p. 13, 16]:

* **Arrive from Reserves:** The player can select one or more Reserves units from their army and set them up on the battlefield, one at a time, according to the rules that placed them in Reserves (such as *Deep Strike*) [Core Rules p. 16].
* **Restrictions & Effects:** Units arriving from Reserves count as having made a Normal move in the turn they are set up; they cannot move further during this phase, but can otherwise act normally later in the turn (shoot, declare a charge, fight) [Core Rules p. 16].

Once all desired Reserves units have been set up, the Movement phase ends [Core Rules p. 16].
